counting_convention.register_record: Concrete addressable register record. FMMU/SyncManager and port-counter arrays are expanded to actual channel addresses. PHY x registers remain templates because the PHY instance is selected through PHY/MII addressing rather than a unique linear ESC address.
counting_convention.memory_region: RAM/window region is counted separately from registers.
counting_convention.register_group: Documentation grouping record is not a concrete register.
counting_convention.bitfield: One documented field row; reserved fields are included.

unconfirmed_and_gaps: No separate public ET1100 errata PDF was located in this investigation; revision/build history is present in the hardware data sheet. Treat absence of a located errata file as a documentation gap, not proof that no errata exists.

No separate LAN9252 product-specific errata document surfaced in the public product-page results investigated. The product page exposes an Errata category, but no concrete LAN9252 errata item was found in the retrieved listing.
A Microchip support search result states LAN9253 currently has no known errata, but this is not a formal silicon-errata PDF; future errata should be checked on the product page.

LAN9253 DS00003421B contains an apparent editorial inconsistency: the Process Data RAM register text includes a 4-KByte wording while the address range/size and product capability are 8 KB. The dataset uses 8 KB and flags this for hardware/document-revision verification.

LAN9253 core section headings retain FMMU[2:0] / SyncManager[3:0] wording in places, while the device capability registers and base-address tables define 8 FMMUs and 8 SyncManagers. The dataset follows the explicit counts/base tables and flags the heading text as editorial inconsistency.

AL-state restrictions are not globally specified for many ESC registers. Where the data sheet gives only hardware conditions (for example SyncManager disabled, EEPROM BUSY clear, DC feature enabled), the dataset records those conditions and leaves AL-state restriction as 'not documented' rather than inventing INIT/PRE-OP/SAFE-OP/OP limits.

Strap-, EEPROM-, silicon-stepping-, and selected-PDI-dependent reset/default values remain conditional where the data sheet does not give one unconditional constant; hardware verification is recommended before using them as UI defaults.
